justifications.c1: The money figures are about escape of water in general, not the problem the sensor fixes: an ABI aggregate of £1.8m/day (Clyde & Co) and an average claim of >£17k (Insurance Times). The losses the sensor addresses are small or vendor-only: one contractor's ~£4/unit-day electricity estimate (Bakers of Danbury), a £600 distress award from one FOS case (DRN-4561814, which search could not find) and a Dantherm vendor model of driving costs.
justifications.c2: Accuserve's blog quotes ANSI/IICRC S500-2021: restorers 'should record and monitor relevant moisture measurements DAILY' until drying goals are met (search-confirmed). The task recurs daily on every live drying job. However, the standard is US, BDMA wording was not found and there is no count of UK jobs per contractor.
justifications.c3: The manual routine is documented: daily moisture and psychrometric logging (Accuserve, R&R, DocuSketch), and contractor-supplied usage details for the electricity refund (Allianz guide, search-confirmed). Its labour or £ cost is quantified only by Dantherm's vendor model (200→80 km per claim).
justifications.c4: The standard is the US IICRC S500. Its 'should' wording is a recommended practice, and no UK requirement or BDMA rule was found. The Allianz guide makes the electricity refund depend on contractor usage details. The FOS cases are about electricity costs and rehousing, not enforcement of monitoring records. 'Insurers dispute run days' was not evidenced.
justifications.c5: The only evidenced titles are restoration technicians (Rainbow International, BELFOR, JobLeads), who hold no budget. No Operations Director or insurer supply-chain manager with a monitoring budget was found (the researcher records this as a gap).
justifications.c6: Panel restoration contractors already install drying kit in the home (Allianz). A UK distributor (National Heater Shops) lists Dantherm Simplify remote humidity monitoring, and hire networks rent dehumidifiers. The channel exists and bundles comparable monitoring, but all of this rests on unverified search extracts.
justifications.c7: The category is crowded: Polygon ReMo, Polygon/Telekom connected dehumidifiers with insurer power reports, Dantherm Simplify, HygroNet, DryTrack (7,000 locations) and Dri-Eaz LGR 5000Li with built-in logging 'to simplify insurance reporting'. Logging is therefore already a feature of equipment buyers own. No prices were found, and the kWh-plug gap is asserted, with no complaint behind it.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf UKCA 13A LoRaWAN metering plugs exist (MOKO LW005-MP $60; Milesight WS523 €86.95), and mains power is easy. A kit needs several plugs per job plus an unpriced LTE-M hub and T/RH and moisture sensors, so the BOM per kit is well over £50. No LTE-M plug was found.
justifications.c9: Each claim needs run-time and drying records (Allianz, S500), so the per-job data stays valuable. Dantherm Simplify includes a 24-month cloud subscription, but no fee is stated, no UK per-job price was found, and hire rates of £16–£50/unit-day cap any add-on price.
justifications.c10: Three source types: insurer loss data (ABI via Clyde & Co and Insurance Times), ombudsman decisions (FOS DRN-4561814, -4694073, 7867279) and trade press (Cleanfax, R&R), plus a Mumsnet thread known by title only. The friction they show is electricity cost and drying duration, not disputed run days, and the key FOS decision could not be found in search.

weakest: The category is mature and already served: Polygon, Dantherm, Dri-Eaz and DryTrack sell remote drying monitoring, and connected dehumidifiers log energy for insurers. The money tied to the specific problem (~£4/unit-day electricity, technician visits) rests on vendor models or tiny amounts.
